High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore

sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri
Manish Jain, learned counsel for the appellant  Shri Arun Gupta, learned counsel for the respondent  ORDER

The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 10.10.2018 passed in claim case No.300/2015 whereby challenging quantum of compensation on the ground of incorrect assessment of income and non-grant of compensation for loss of consortium.
2. The short facts of the case are that on 09.09.2014, the deceased Alpesh was going, sitting in Tavera vehicle bearing registration number MP09-BD- 0708, to his home along with his friend.

When they reached near village- Madad at Indore-Ahemdabad road, a Tanker bearing registration number MP44-HA-0212 came, the driver of which was driving the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into Tavera vehicle in which Alpesh was sitting because of which he sustained grievous injuries and died at the spot itself.
He was 23 years of age at the time of accident and was studying in 2 MA-464-2019 B.Com 1st year.
He had cleared B.Com 1st year at the time of accident.
3. The appellants, who are mother and father of the deceased Alpesh filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for his death.

The claims tribunal after recording evidence concluded that the driver of the insured vehicle was driving the same in a rash and negligent manner, thus, awarded total compensation of Rs.7,86,000/- to the appellants and liability of the same was fixed on the insurance company.
4.

The learned counsel for the appellants submits that while calculating the compensation the claims tribunal discarded the claim of the appellants that the deceased was a bright student and was preparing for CA, thus, he should be treated as skilled person and accordingly his income should be assessed.
On notional basis, Rs.5000/- was treated as his income by treating him as an unskilled labourer, which is not correct.
He further submits that nothing has been awarded for loss of consortium whereas the claimants are mother and father of the deceased.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/insurance company submits that the deceased was 23 years of age and had cleared 12th examination only with second division.

At the age of 23 years,
he was still pursuing his B.Com and had cleared only first year which is late as per the trajectory of a regular student.
As such this cannot be presumed that he was having a bright academic future.
As such, the claims tribunal has correctly assessed his income.
6. Learned counsel further submits that the amount of compensation as awarded by the Tribunal is a just compensation, hence, no interference is warranted in the impugned award.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.

From perusal of the record, it is seen that Ex.P-13 is the mark-sheet of class 3 MA-464-2019 12th of deceased Alpesh which he has cleared in second division and he has also cleared B.Com. 1st year which is not under dispute.

The claims tribunal has treated him as an unskilled labourer without noticing the fact that undeniably he was a student who had already cleared upto higher secondary and was pursuing his studies for graduation in which he has cleared 1st year also, thus, treating him as an unskilled labourer would not be appropriate in the considered view of this Court.

However, in view of the marks scored in mark-sheet Ex.P-13, this Court is of the considered view that the income of the deceased boy has to be taken by considering the wages spectrum of unskilled to skilled labourer.
For unskilled labourer the minimum wages are Rs.5845/- and for skilled Rs.6,125/-.

Thus,
the income of the deceased in the peculiar facts of the present case is taken as Rs.6000/- per month.
Consequently, the amount of compensation for loss of dependency is hereby changed to Rs.9,07,200/- by applying all other factors as applied by the claims tribunal.

9. As regards the compensation for loss of consortium in view of the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram, AIR OnLine 2018 SC 1249, mother and father are entitled for compensation.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram, AIR OnLine 2018 SC 1249
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, both are hereby awarded Rs.40,000/- each.

In view of the additions and modifications, the total compensation now comes to Rs.10,17,200/- and after deducting already awarded amount of Rs.7,86,000/-, the appellants are entitled for payment of Rs.2,31,200/- which shall be paid to them over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @6% per annum from the date of the application before the claims tribunal.

In view of the fact that the matter relates to compensation for death son of appellants, the excess court fees which has been paid by them is hereby directed to be refunded considering the enhancement of compensation of Rs.2,31,200/-.
11.
With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed of.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
